slides.title: Introduction to DRF
slides.content:
# Django REST Framework 🔌

Build powerful, flexible Web APIs!

## What you'll learn:
- **Django REST Framework** - Overview and setup
- **Creating APIs with DRF** - ViewSets and Views
- **Serializers, Views, and Routers** - Core concepts

## What is REST?

```
REST = REpresentational State Transfer

HTTP Methods → CRUD Operations:
GET    → Read
POST   → Create
PUT    → Update (full)
PATCH  → Update (partial)
DELETE → Delete
```

## Installation

```bash
pip install djangorestframework
```

```python
# settings.py
INSTALLED_APPS = [
    ...
    'rest_framework',
]

# Optional: Global settings
REST_FRAMEWORK = {
    'DEFAULT_PERMISSION_CLASSES': [
        'rest_framework.permissions.IsAuthenticated',
    ],
    'DEFAULT_PAGINATION_CLASS': 'rest_framework.pagination.PageNumberPagination',
    'PAGE_SIZE': 10,
}
```

> 💡 **DRF is the industry standard** for building APIs in Django!

slides.title: Serializers
slides.content:
# Serializers 📦

Convert complex data to JSON and vice versa!

## ModelSerializer (Most Common)

```python
# serializers.py
from rest_framework import serializers
from .models import Article, Category

class ArticleSerializer(serializers.ModelSerializer):
    class Meta:
        model = Article
        fields = ['id', 'title', 'content', 'author', 'published']
        # Or: fields = '__all__'
        # Or: exclude = ['draft_content']
        read_only_fields = ['author', 'published']
```

## Nested Serializers

```python
class CategorySerializer(serializers.ModelSerializer):
    class Meta:
        model = Category
        fields = ['id', 'name', 'slug']

class ArticleSerializer(serializers.ModelSerializer):
    category = CategorySerializer(read_only=True)  # Nested!
    author_name = serializers.CharField(source='author.username', read_only=True)
    
    class Meta:
        model = Article
        fields = ['id', 'title', 'content', 'category', 'author_name']
```

## Custom Validation

```python
class ArticleSerializer(serializers.ModelSerializer):
    class Meta:
        model = Article
        fields = ['title', 'content']
    
    def validate_title(self, value):
        if len(value) < 5:
            raise serializers.ValidationError('Title too short')
        return value
    
    def validate(self, data):
        if 'spam' in data['content'].lower():
            raise serializers.ValidationError('Spam detected')
        return data
```

> 💡 **Serializers = Forms for APIs!** They handle validation and conversion.

slides.title: API Views
ViewSets and Routers
slides.content:
# ViewSets & Routers 🚀

Combine all CRUD operations in one class!

## ViewSet

```python
# views.py
from rest_framework import viewsets
from .models import Article
from .serializers import ArticleSerializer

class ArticleViewSet(viewsets.ModelViewSet):
    queryset = Article.objects.all()
    serializer_class = ArticleSerializer
    
    # Optional: Filter by user
    def get_queryset(self):
        return Article.objects.filter(author=self.request.user)
    
    # Optional: Set author on create
    def perform_create(self, serializer):
        serializer.save(author=self.request.user)
```

## Router (Auto-generates URLs!)

```python
# urls.py
from rest_framework.routers import DefaultRouter
from .views import ArticleViewSet, CategoryViewSet

router = DefaultRouter()
router.register('articles', ArticleViewSet)
router.register('categories', CategoryViewSet)

urlpatterns = [
    path('api/', include(router.urls)),
]

# Auto-generates:
# GET    /api/articles/      → list
# POST   /api/articles/      → create
# GET    /api/articles/{id}/ → retrieve
# PUT    /api/articles/{id}/ → update
# PATCH  /api/articles/{id}/ → partial update
# DELETE /api/articles/{id}/ → destroy
```

> 💡 **ViewSet + Router = Full CRUD API** with minimal code!

slides.title: Authentication & Permissions
slides.content:
# API Security 🔐

## Permission Classes

```python
from rest_framework import permissions

class ArticleViewSet(viewsets.ModelViewSet):
    queryset = Article.objects.all()
    serializer_class = ArticleSerializer
    
    # Require authentication
    permission_classes = [permissions.IsAuthenticated]
    
    # Or multiple permissions
    permission_classes = [
        permissions.IsAuthenticated,
        permissions.IsAdminUser,
    ]
```

## Built-in Permissions

| Permission | Description |
|------------|-------------|
| `AllowAny` | No restrictions |
| `IsAuthenticated` | Must be logged in |
| `IsAdminUser` | Must be staff |
| `IsAuthenticatedOrReadOnly` | Read for all, write for logged in |

## Custom Permissions

```python
class IsAuthorOrReadOnly(permissions.BasePermission):
    def has_object_permission(self, request, view, obj):
        # Read permissions for any request
        if request.method in permissions.SAFE_METHODS:
            return True
        # Write permissions only for author
        return obj.author == request.user
```

## Token Authentication

```python
# settings.py
REST_FRAMEWORK = {
    'DEFAULT_AUTHENTICATION_CLASSES': [
        'rest_framework.authentication.TokenAuthentication',
    ]
}

# Generate token for user
from rest_framework.authtoken.models import Token
token = Token.objects.create(user=user)

# Client sends: Authorization: Token <token>
```

slides.title: Summary
slides.content:
# Excellent Work! 🎉

You've mastered Django REST Framework!

## Django REST Framework
- ✅ Install with `pip install djangorestframework`
- ✅ Add to `INSTALLED_APPS`
- ✅ Browse API at `/api/`

## Serializers
- ✅ `ModelSerializer` for quick setup
- ✅ Nested serializers for relationships
- ✅ Validation with `validate_<field>()`

## Creating APIs with DRF
- ✅ `@api_view` for function views
- ✅ `APIView` for class-based
- ✅ `generics` for common patterns

## ViewSets and Routers
- ✅ `ModelViewSet` for full CRUD
- ✅ `DefaultRouter` auto-generates URLs
- ✅ Permission classes for security
- ✅ Token authentication

## Quick API Setup

```python
# Serializer
class ArticleSerializer(serializers.ModelSerializer):
    class Meta:
        model = Article
        fields = '__all__'

# ViewSet
class ArticleViewSet(viewsets.ModelViewSet):
    queryset = Article.objects.all()
    serializer_class = ArticleSerializer

# Router
router.register('articles', ArticleViewSet)
```

> 🚀 **Next Steps:** Learn about Middleware!
